sourceInformation.genre: Life Sim (with a timing-based pitch minigame)
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.85.1 (inlined, MIT); JavaScript; Canvas 2D; hub client session.js 1.3.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Pixel art in the engine's SNES-style 3/4 view, a 1963 office palette
sourceInformation.audio: Chip-synth music and sound effects from the engine; no voice work
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub parallel session, 1 to 4 players; progress and result only
sourceInformation.testing: 21 rules tests and 65 engine checks (headless, including a three-day bot playthrough); AI Hub harness with 2 and 4 players (4 with latency and loss); viewport matrix at 24 sizes in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); Chromium for checks
sourceInformation.usage: cost unknown; about 0.29M tokens by the session budget counter (breakdown unknown); about 14 minutes

testingFeedback: 7 issues in the game: the attract demo never reached the boardroom; the pitch prompt sat on the box border; the summary log ran into its prompt; the credits ran past the right edge; the middle dot showed as a question mark; the scroll hint showed raw letters; the touch-only message could never show.
0 critical. None of the 7 was game-breaking; the demo one stopped the attract mode from showing a pitch.
The headless three-day bot playthrough, driven by the same inputs a player sends, through to an ending.
The first viewport-matrix run, which hit another agent's page on the same port and so tested the wrong game. Port checks came first after that.
engineFeedback: E.Dialog with portraits and choices, E.Shell's HTML HUD, settings.define for game options, and TileMap rows with floorTex.
The default font has no middle dot, so it drew as a question mark. The engine starts with lastDevice set to keyboard, so a touch-only phone does not look touch-only until it is touched.
The office floor plan, the day and encounter rules, the pitch minigame, the endings, the attract AI, and the hub session flow.
At expand the internal screen is about 225 pixels tall, so small text needs care.
The default font glyph set, with a glyph test in the engine.
lastDevice starting as unknown rather than keyboard.
promptFeedback: The concrete deliverable list, the hub and engine links, and the done rule.
"Silently brainstorm" sits awkwardly with the RNG step, which needed a visible list in a tool call; "Source" and "Source Information" overlap.
Fitting attract mode, the hub round, glyphs, inversion, touch rules and tests into one session.
A real DualSense on a real iPhone, not an emulator.

aiHub.name: Mad Men at Large
aiHub.description: Three days, three client pitches and one bottle too many. Stats pull against each other, and a timing-based pitch decides each account.
aiHub.controls: WASD or stick walks; E talks and pours; Q smokes; Enter or A pitches; Esc pauses
